text.p: Folllowing are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New protective taxes on some 50 kinds of imported groceries including cheese and fresh fruit and vegetables lifts their price in Croatian shops.
- President Franjo Tudjman meets British Foreign Minister Robin Cook who expressed a wish to see Croatia integrated within modern Europe.

- Croatian army general Ivan Korade, who was the first one to hang the Croatian flag on Knin fortress when government troops recaptured it from rebel Serbs in 1995, has been arrested after a series of excesses, government sources say.
- Croatian police set an August 19 deadline for citizens to hand over all personal weapons, without a special licence, which they have been allowed to hold since 1991.
- Farmers in Varazdin county suffered 10 million kuna worth of damage in recent hail storms. Most of the corn crops, vegetables and vineyards were completely destroyed.
- Croatian fans spent all night in the streets of Zagreb celebrating the landslide victory (5-0) of their soccer team Croatia, formerly known as Dinamo, over Belgrade's Partizan.
- New U.N. administrator William Walker will take charge of Croatia's last mostly Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia in mid-August, UN spokesman Philip Arnold said.

- Dubrovnik shipper Jadranska Plovidba signs contract for a $35.4 million loan from Hamburgische Landesbank, director of Atlantska Ante Jerkovic says. The loan will be used to refinance old debts and upgrade the fleet.
- "I could not have imagined such a defeat," says director of Yugoslav soccer team Nenad Bjekovic after his team was beaten by Croatia in Zagreb 5-0.
- Blaze still alive on the island of Hvar where 3,000 hectares of pinewood, brush and farmland have been burned since Monday.

- Trade Union Association SSSH accepts the introduction of VAT is due, but will ask the government to introduce some measures to protect living standards, SSSH president Davor Juric said. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
